ranked_facts.why: The presence of granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels, as indicated by direct immunofluorescence, is more characteristic of Linear or Annular Lupus Erythematosus Panniculitis of the Scalp (LALPS) than of other conditions like Scarring Alopecia, Neoplastic Scalp Disease, Infectious Scalp Disease, or Other conditions.

The scanning view showing predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis is more indicative of Linear or Annular Lupus Erythematosus Panniculitis of the Scalp (LALPS) than of other conditions.
